name: vss_materialise
description: Copy chosen files out of chosen volume shadow copies of a raw volume or disk image, under the tool's own output, each tagged with the snapshot it came from. vshadowinfo lists the stores (identifier, creation time); vshadowmount (FUSE) exposes each selected store as a file vssN under a directory of this tool's own (work/<agent id>/, or $OUT in a job); a path is found in it component by component with the Sleuth Kit's fls (case-insensitively, no deleted entry taken, no link followed: the volume is read as a volume) and copied with icat. The mount is that VM's alone and is not a sealed output; it is unmounted in a finally, at the tool's own deadline, and on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal), and the answer says whether the unmount could be shown. Without FUSE (/dev/fuse that cannot be opened, or neither fusermount3 nor fusermount) the answer is JSON with blocked: no FUSE, status failed and a no_fuse object, and nothing is written; that is a limit of the VM, never a finding about the evidence. Inputs: image (a raw volume or disk image, or a device file; an E01 has to be exposed raw first), offset in BYTES, stores (the store numbers vss_stores lists), paths (from the volume root, / or \ separated, at most 32 components, no . or .., no line break), max_copy_bytes (default 2 GiB; a larger file is not copied and is named), limit (rows inline; every row is in the file rows_file names), copy_credentials. The answer says which store has which path (paths_in_stores), and per path and store a row: found, copy_status (copied, not_in_store, credential_file_not_copied, too_large, listing_too_large, read_failed, write_failed, timeout, not_regular, store_not_exposed or not_attempted), the file's inode, the copy's place, size and sha256, the store's number, identifier and creation time, and relation_to_live (same, differs or absent_in_live, from reading the same path in the volume as it is now; not_compared for a credential file, when the offset is not a multiple of 512, when the clock ran out, when the live lookup or read failed or timed out, and when the live file is over max_copy_bytes). A path absent from a store is a fact about that snapshot, not a failure; a store number vshadowinfo does not list, a failed lookup or copy, a lookup the clock cut off and a mount that could not be shown to be gone make the answer partial and are named. A copy is written to a hidden file, hashed as it is written and placed without replacing an earlier file (a rerun keeps what was there); a copy that could not be written whole (a full disk, a quota, the size cap, the clock, a signal) is removed and is never named as a copy, and a refused write stops the copying and says nothing about the evidence. SAM, SECURITY and NTDS.dit are credential files: they are looked up, and copied only on copy_credentials: true, which is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1) and refused as JSON before anything is made elsewhere; the digest of a credential file is computed in memory while it is copied, and is never printed or written, and without copy_credentials one that is found is named credential_file_not_copied. A directory listing from fls is read to at most 16 MiB; a larger one stops fls and the path is named listing_too_large. The mount is waited for once, 5 seconds in all, never store by store; a store file that is not there then is store_not_exposed. If a signal cut the unmount short, the last word tries a lazy unmount (-u -z) once more and says so. Programs run in the tool's own process group (never a session of its own) and are killed with what they started at the deadline. One clock covers the run: copying stops 25 seconds before its 270, and the unmount and the answer come inside it (the manifest allows 300). The answer's copies is the number of files copied, row_count the number of rows. Every answer carries status and status_basis. Listing a snapshot is not examining it. NOT verified here: a run against a real shadow copy and a real FUSE mount; the tool is exercised against stand-ins for vshadowinfo, vshadowmount, fusermount, fls and icat that follow their documented output.

image.description: A raw volume or disk image, or a device file (not an E01: expose it raw first)

stores.description: Store numbers to open, as vss_stores lists them (1 to 64 whole numbers from 1)

paths.description: Paths inside the volume to copy out of each store, from its root: /Windows/System32/config/SYSTEM (1 to 200)

max_copy_bytes.description: Largest file to copy (default 2147483648); a larger one is named and not copied

limit.description: Rows shown inline (default 100); every row is in the file named by rows_file

copy_credentials.description: Also copy SAM, SECURITY and NTDS.dit (no digest is printed or written): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
